'''2014 World Championship''' was the 19th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] in Toronto, Ontario, on 21–24 August 2014.<ref name="awards" /><ref name="format" /> 31 players took part.<ref name="wp" /> [[Emil Wallin]] defeated [[Brian Terwilliger]] (forum name Brian Twigg) in the final, playing Wookiee Slaving Operation and Mind What You Have Learned on Day 3, and became the third player to win two World Championships after [[Jonny Chu]] and [[Kevin Shannon]] (2012 and 2014).<ref name="finals">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=55897 FINALS], forum.starwarsccg.org (24 August 2014). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022033406/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t55897.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="awards" /> The main event used [[Premiere - Virtual Block 9.1]]; the Players Committee had decided not to release Virtual Block 9.2 in its July 2014 form and announced a mini, 12-card set for Worlds instead.<ref name="reset">[https://web.archive.org/web/20141020142523/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/wp/reset-of-standard-format/ Reset of Standard Format], starwarsccg.org (25 July 2014), Internet Archive copy.</ref> A separate [[2014 World Championship Reset Beta|Reset Beta]] side event tried out the post-reset card pool.<ref name="format" />

== Results ==

Places follow the Day 3 bracket below; semifinal and quarterfinal losers are shown as ties. Decks are the Day 3 lists. Chris Terwilliger, [[Aaron Kingery]], and [[Brian Terwilliger]] turned in Day 3 OUT/IN change sheets. Chris's submitted Dark 60 is page 1 of the Day 3 PDF (not in the Day 2 parts); that 60 and the change sheet are both on his Dark article. Aaron and Brian's submitted 60s are in the Day 2 PDFs and are copied onto their Day 3 articles.

=== Top 8 bracket ===

Day 3 pairings as posted by raith (seeds in brackets):<ref name="day3">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=55887 Day 3], forum.starwarsccg.org (raith, 23 August 2014). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022025229/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t55887.html Internet Archive]</ref>

* Quarterfinals: (1) [[Emil Wallin]] def. (8) [[Aaron Kingery]] 2–0; (4) [[Angelo Consoli]] def. (5) [[Chris Terwilliger]]; (6) [[Brian Terwilliger]] def. (3) [[Matt Sokol]]; (2) [[Matthew Harrison-Trainor]] def. (7) [[Greg Shaw]]
* Semifinals: Emil Wallin def. Angelo Consoli; Brian Terwilliger def. Matthew Harrison-Trainor
* Final: Emil Wallin def. Brian Terwilliger

Only the Kingery quarterfinal score was posted; the other quarterfinal winners follow from the semifinal line-up.<ref name="day3" /> Live reports: Brian game 1 over MHT by 34 (Mon Cals over walkers); Angelo game 1 by 13 (A Stunning Move over Mind What You Have Learned).<ref name="day3" /> Final, game 1: Emil Light by 6 on time.<ref name="finals" /> The full final score was not posted.

== Day 2 ==

Emil went 3–1. [[Matt Sokol]] beat the Imperial Entanglements list by destroying Devastator and putting Legendary Starfighter on the Falcon.<ref name="emil">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=55902 World Champions Decklists], forum.starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022032443/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t55902.html Internet Archive]</ref> Chris Terwilliger's Day 2 Dark was never in the zip (Advocate, t=56104).

=== Reset Beta ===
